title: Cross-verifier adversarial qualification
canonical_definition: Cover forged/replayed verdicts, stale policy, wrong job/worker/attempt, verifier collusion, authority drift and failure atomicity.
user_shorthand: False verifier, colluding verifier, replayed verdict, altered output, wrong worker, wrong job, stale policy, etc.

roadmap_order.note: CMP-1.4.4 remains open. CMP-1.4.10 adversarially qualifies the currently implemented verifier surfaces but does not retroactively claim the separate signed-verdict minimum-binding step complete.

implementation.rationale: CMP-1.4.10 is an adversarial qualification step. Existing production guards are retained; the only code change is stronger failure-atomicity assertion coverage for stale/duplicate policy binding.

threat_matrix.note: The signed verdict binds the canonical assignmentRef; WorkerSnapshot tests separately prove cross-worker/cross-attempt replay rejection on the authoritative execution evidence.

authority_boundaries: Rejected verifier actions must not mutate canonical job state, burn a nonce that belongs to a rejected verdict, release payer backing, create an entitlement, or alter a frozen policy/adapter route.
Verifier identity, capability, selection, correctness evidence, dispute review and settlement remain separate authorities under hostile inputs.
Shared-controller or provider-friendly verifier sets fail closed; threshold counting never converts duplicate/colluding votes into independent quorum.
Later policy/adapter publication does not rewrite accepted historical semantics; stale attempts cannot silently rebind a job.
A worker/result/assignment mismatch cannot be repaired by a valid verifier signature.
Challenge/appeal state cannot rewrite the original verifier decision or create stake/slash authority.
Scientific/deterministic evidence families cannot masquerade as one another.
No adversarial test may pass by weakening authorization, replay, policy, independence, settlement or failure-atomicity guards.

milestone_relationship.rationale: The canonical step is itself a cross-verifier adversarial qualification boundary spanning signed verdicts, policy binding, worker evidence, independent selection, quorum, deterministic/scientific adapters and dispute hooks. The retained full Compute suite is therefore required on the exact implementation SHA.

exit_criteria: Every canonical CMP-1.4.10 threat class is mapped to at least one exact executable test.
Forged/false verifier and hostile signed-verdict fields fail closed without state/economic mutation.
Verdict replay, expiry and cross-domain replay fail closed.
Wrong job/result/assignment/output and cross-job evidence substitutions fail closed.
Wrong worker/cross-worker/wrong attempt/stale attempt evidence cannot replay into verification.
Stale/disabled/mutated verification policy cannot replace the accepted frozen policy; rejected stale/duplicate binding is failure-atomic.
Friendly/shared-controller/colluding verifier arrangements cannot satisfy independence/quorum requirements.
Authority, controller, capability, selector or verifier lifecycle drift fails closed where current eligibility is required.
Deterministic/scientific adapter-family substitution and evaluation replay fail closed.
Challenge/appeal authority confusion cannot rewrite verdicts, release held entitlement prematurely or mint slash authority.
Rejected hostile paths preserve canonical state, nonce/evidence semantics and payer/provider isolation.
Level 1 exact-head mechanical threat-matrix verification is green.
Level 2 retained Compute adversarial/integration suite is green on the same exact implementation SHA.
